reason: The text demonstrates agency exercised by multiple non-leader figures. Moses, initially only a shepherd (not a leader), independently chooses to turn aside and investigate the burning bush ('וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אָסֻֽרָה־ נָּא וְאֶרְאֶה'—'I will turn aside and see'). Additionally, the Israelites themselves are portrayed as possessing agency through their collective cry or plea ('צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל'—'the cry of the children of Israel'), which prompts God's response. The text shows that agency belongs to ordinary people and even non-leaders, not exclusively to those in leadership positions.
